attendees.role: board member (addressed by a commenter as handling the surplus account)

public_comment.topic: Follow-up on the general surplus account, whether PFAS settlement money is properly segregated, and whether the district is exceeding a statutory cap on surplus funds (MGL c.41 s.69B / the 1939 charter).

votes.motion: Approve the minutes for the special meeting of February 25th and the regular meeting of February 25th.

budget_items.what_was_said: The food pantry representative said the district would have to raise money to build a new building rather than pay for land, since the town would only give land, not funds.

budget_items.topic: Water main route savings via easement
budget_items.what_was_said: Running the transmission main through private land (cross-country easement) rather than along town roads was estimated to save a large distance versus going through center town toward Lancaster.
The superintendent reported the district is on the state's SRF funding list again, but this round offers loans rather than the previous zero-percent, principal-forgiveness terms.

budget_items.topic: PFAS treatment plant contingency and water main work savings
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said if water main work around the treatment plant and wells is done efficiently and stays in budget, savings could be redirected to fund the raw water transmission main.
The superintendent reported that a new Caterpillar excavator would be too large and priced above what the district wants to spend; used equipment is being considered instead.

budget_items.topic: General surplus account balance and prior allocations
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident recalled the account held roughly $1.1 million before the board voted to allocate funds for meter readers, an excavator, and a retroactive Medicare payment shortfall covering two years, leaving roughly $815,000.

budget_items.topic: PFAS litigation settlement money within surplus
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked whether roughly $250,000 of PFAS litigation settlement money sitting in the general surplus account is separately tracked; the superintendent said it is flagged internally as PFAS money though commingled in the same account.

budget_items.topic: Statutory cap on water district surplus
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident raised that the district's 1939 charter and Massachusetts General Law may cap unallocated surplus at a set figure, with any excess required to be returned to ratepayers via rate reductions; the board said it would look into it.
A commissioner asked about the balance in the cellular tower account, which has been accruing interest not reflected in the district's budget figures.

transfers.description: Potential transfer of savings from treatment-plant-area water main work into funding the raw water transmission main
Interest earned on the cell tower account/CDs proposed to be put toward replacing water mains

decisions.decision: Annual meeting voting hours will change to 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Saturday, March 28th, with the business meeting paused during voting and results announced at 4 p.m.
No absentee or early voting will be offered, per advice from the district's attorney and town counsel that it is not legally available to a water district.
Future correspondence from the Citizens for Affordable Clean Water group should be brought to the board via the meeting agenda or public comment rather than as direct emails to the superintendent.

The developer proposing the water district expansion article will be invited to present information to the public before the annual meeting, though the board has no authority over the substance of the proposal.
The board agreed to look into how surplus funds, PFAS settlement money, and interest income should be tracked and allocated, in light of the statutory surplus question raised in public comment.

minutes.headline: Resident says water district's surplus fund may violate the $100,000 statutory cap on district reserves.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners heard the Community Food Pantry's search for a new building site, discussed easement negotiations and PFAS treatment funding, changed annual-meeting voting hours, and agreed to route future citizen-group correspondence through public meetings. In public comment, a resident questioned whether the district's general surplus account -- including commingled PFAS settlement money -- exceeds a legal cap on unallocated surplus, and the board agreed to look into it.
